finding.claim: href() appends an unvalidated optionalPort (typed number|string) into a URL and returns it unescaped; an untrusted string port can inject URL authority or break out of an HTML attribute. Severity: medium, conditional on caller passing untrusted string.
finding.source: optionalPort parameter of Address6.href(), typed number | string, caller-controlled
finding.sink: Returned URL string http://[...]:<port>/ (src/ipv6.ts:1458), commonly embedded into HTML href attributes or fetch URLs

trace.note: optionalPort = `:${optionalPort}` with no digit or character validation
returned as http://[${correctForm()}]${optionalPort}/ with no escaping

finding.guards_checked: correctForm() output is digits and hex only, so the address part is safe. The port is not validated, not range-checked, and not HTML-escaped. Contrast with link() at src/ipv6.ts:1493-1494, which does escapeHtml.

finding.claim: simpleGroup() returns any group containing 'group-v4' without escaping, so arbitrary text containing that substring reaches HTML output raw. Reachable through the public v6.helpers export. Severity: low-medium.
finding.source: addressString argument of exported helpers.simpleGroup, reachable via src/index.ts:7 (export const v6 = { helpers })
finding.sink: HTML fragment returned to the caller (src/v6/helpers.ts:53 passthrough)

trace.note: helpers module imported and exported publicly

finding.guards_checked: Non-matching groups go through escapeHtml at src/v6/helpers.ts:32 and :56. Internal callers in src/ipv6.ts:1517, :1529, :1543 pass only parse-validated addresses, which cannot contain 'group-v4' because 'g','r','o','u','p','v' fail RE_BAD_CHARACTERS. The gap is only for external callers passing raw text.

finding.claim: embeddedIPv4() unwraps only IPv4-mapped and NAT64 well-known addresses. 6to4 (2002::/16) and IPv4-compatible (::/96) addresses embedding a private or loopback IPv4 are classed as Global by isLoopback(), isPrivate(), isCGNAT() and isBroadcast(). This defeats the SSRF allow/deny use case the doc at lines 1306-1316 describes. Severity: low-medium, conditional on the host routing 6to4 to the embedded IPv4.
finding.source: Attacker-supplied IPv6 literal such as 2002:7f00:1:: or ::7f00:1
finding.sink: Trust-boundary classifiers isLoopback/isPrivate (src/ipv6.ts:1345-1352, :1380-1387) used as SSRF allow/deny decisions

trace.note: embeddedIPv4 checks only isMapped4() or NAT64_WELL_KNOWN_SUBNET
getType() returns '6to4' (src/v6/constants.ts:50), so !== 'Loopback' and result is false
isPrivate: isULA() and NAT64 local-use both false, so result is false

finding.guards_checked: Mapped and NAT64 embedding is handled correctly. The 6to4 gateway is available via inspect6to4() (src/ipv6.ts:1017-1031) but no classifier uses it. The doc at ipv6.ts:1306-1316 lists only mapped and NAT64 as embeddings.

finding.claim: isLinkLocal() requires the first 64 bits to be exactly fe80:0:0:0, so fe80:0:0:1::1 is not link-local here, while getType() (via fe80::/10 in src/v6/constants.ts:48) reports 'Link-local unicast'. The two classifiers disagree. Severity: low.
finding.source: Attacker-supplied IPv6 literal such as fe80:0:0:1::1
finding.sink: isLinkLocal() return value used as a trust-boundary or ACL classification

trace.note: isLinkLocal: embeddedIPv4() is null for fe80::
compares getBitsBase2(0,64) to the exact string for fe80:0000:0000:0000
getType() uses isHostInSubnet against fe80::/10 and returns 'Link-local unicast'

finding.guards_checked: The comment at src/ipv6.ts:1252 acknowledges the zero-bit check as deliberate. Under RFC 4291 the 54 bits after the prefix are zero, so this is mainly an internal inconsistency rather than a clear bypass.

finding.claim: fromUnsignedByteArray does not type-check elements, so a JS caller passing [10,0,0,'1/8'] gets 10.0.0.1/8 with subnetMask 8 silently. The doc says values outside 0-255 are rejected. Severity: low, only for untyped JS callers with untrusted arrays.
finding.source: bytes argument of Address4.fromUnsignedByteArray, e.g. untrusted JSON parsed into an array
finding.sink: Address4 construction; resulting subnetMask changes the prefix used by containment and classification checks

trace.note: fromUnsignedByteArray entry, no assertByteArray call (unlike fromByteArray at :385)

finding.guards_checked: fromByteArray at src/ipv4.ts:384-385 calls common.assertByteArray and rejects non-integers. The unsigned variant skips that check. TypeScript typing prevents this for typed callers only.

finding.claim: fromURL() returns {address: null} for URLs with userinfo, backslashes or other non-IP-literal syntax such as http://user@[::1]/. The result cannot distinguish 'not an IP literal' from 'malformed', so a caller that treats null as 'hostname, allow' fails open. API footgun, low severity.
finding.source: url argument of Address6.fromURL, attacker-controlled URL string
finding.sink: Caller allow/deny decision that treats null as not-internal, followed by a real HTTP client that resolves the URL to [::1]

trace.note: bracket branch requires ']:' which is absent
RE_URL host class [0-9a-f:.] rejects 'u' and '@' before '[', so no match
return { error, address: null, port: null }

finding.guards_checked: The regex is anchored and the host is validated by new Address6 at src/ipv6.ts:262-266, so no wrong address is returned. The gap is the null-as-hostname interpretation by the caller.
